title: Elasticsearch: documents, indices, shards
description: Elasticsearch stores JSON documents in indices, distributed across shards and replicas for scale and resilience. An index is a logical namespace; shards are the physical split. The architecture is what lets one cluster hold billions of documents.

demo.program: print('index -> shards + replicas -> billions of docs')

title: Inverted indexes under the hood
description: Both engines index text with inverted indexes (term -> document list), inherited from Apache Lucene in Elasticsearch's case. Tokenization, stemming, and stop words happen at index time via analyzers. Understanding the inverted index explains relevance scoring.

title: Mappings: schema for your JSON
description: Elasticsearch mappings declare field types (text vs keyword, dates, geo) controlling how fields index and query. Dynamic mapping guesses; explicit mapping is production practice. Keyword fields aggregate, text fields search.
